From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: POC kickoff: scope, success criteria, and model recommendation for MediSys

Hi Elaine / Samir —

Thanks again for the productive demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the POC scope: 

Recap of needs
- Assist clinical support agents with summarization + triage of inbound messages and attachments
- High throughput during business hours (~8k–12k QA interactions/month initially)
- Multilingual support for English, Latin American Spanish, and French (low-volume for FR)
- Strong hallucination controls on clinical/factual output and strict audit trail for outputs

Proposed POC scope (2-week focused trial)
- Dataset: subset of anonymized ticket history (200 representative threads) + 100 doc samples for retrieval testing
- Models: primary: Mistral-7B-instruct (fp16) tuned for instruction-following; fallback: Llama2-7B-chat q4 (lower-cost quantized)
  - Rationale: Mistral-7B shows best mix of latency and instruction quality on short answer tasks in our benchmarks; fallback preserves throughput when capacity tightens
- Multilingual strategy: single-model approach for EN/ES with targeted prompt templates; if FR quality lagging, route FR to a separate FR-specialist checkpoint (TBD)
- SLAs: p50 latency target < 300ms for single-turn queries, p95 < 900ms for retrieval-augmented responses

Success criteria (must-pass & stretch)
- Must-pass: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on labeled test set; factual hallucination rate <= 3% on spot checks; audit logs complete for 100% of requests
- Stretch: automated triage accuracy (top-1 match to gold label) >= 88%; average token cost reduction >= 20% vs current baseline

Evaluation plan
- Week 0 (prep): deliver anonymized sample dataset + security questionnaire; Redwood provides eval rubric template and synthetic baseline run
- Week 1 (trial): Redwood runs inference on sample set; automated metrics + 10 human spot-checks per model variant
- Week 2 (wrap): joint review session, export of logs & metrics; decision: proceed to dedicated pilot or iterate on prompts/model selection

Ownership and roles
- Redwood PM/lead: Marcus Lin (me) — overall POC owner, weekly syncs
- Redwood security lead: Tessa Morgan — security & SOC2 questions, access controls
- Redwood ML lead: Neha Kapoor — model config, evals, prompt engineering
- MediSys: data owner & clinical SME — provide anonymized data and acceptance signoff

Immediate asks for MediSys
1) Confirm you can deliver the de-identified sample dataset by Mon 24 May
2) Confirm Latin American Spanish coverage requirement (regional variants)
3) Point us to your security contact for the questionnaire (Tessa will reach out)

Attachments: I attached the POC template and a spreadsheet with preliminary success metrics (see filenames). I also linked a short HubSpot record for the deal.

Proposed kickoff: Tue 25 May, 10:00–11:00 PT — fine to confirm?

Thanks,

Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the clear plan, this looks good. A few clarifying questions before we commit to the proposed window: 

1) Data residency & compliance: for the initial 2-week trial, are we ok to run on Redwood hosted (US) with encryption-at-rest and in-transit? For production we may need a VPC/private deployment — would that be a blocker for the POC?

2) Spanish: yes, Latin American Spanish is the target (Mexico/Colombia variants). We can provide ~50 threads in Spanish for the sample set. Will the single-model approach you suggested be sufficient or do you expect separate regional tuning?

3) Timeline: we can deliver the anonymized sample by Mon 24 May if you confirm the data schema you need (ticket text, tags, ISO timestamps, attachments metadata).

Also we need an estimate of expected cost for the 2-week run and whether you provide any trial credits. Samir and I will review the success metrics workbook and get back with any edits.

Best,

Hi Elaine / Samir —

Quick answers from security:
- Hosted (US) is fine for the short 2-week eval if you provide de-identified data and sign the minimal DPA addendum we shared last quarter. For anything beyond the POC or PHI-bearing datasets, we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or Dedicated capacity.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest + TLS1.3 in transit; logs and keys handled via customer-managed KMS for Private deployments.
- Evidence: I'll attach a short SOC2 summary in the kickoff packet; if you need the full report we'll route an NDA and an audit access window.

On Spanish/regional variants: our initial approach is single-model with prompt templates. If you see consistent degradation in Latin American variants during Week 1, we'll spin a small in-domain tune or use a language-specific checkpoint for FR/ES. That plan keeps costs down while preserving a fast iteration loop.

Cost & credits: Marcus — can you confirm trial credit policy here? I believe we can offer a small hosted credit for this POC; I'll flag with finance if necessary.
